approvalNotes: Example artifact for validating the Visual Concept Gate. Not an approved direction.

concepts.name: Specimen Wall
concepts.visualMetaphor: A premium workshop wall where each robot is presented like a rare physical specimen rather than a SaaS card.
concepts.composition: One oversized selected robot anchors the left side while a tight vertical rail of smaller robot specimens creates comparison without turning into a catalog.
concepts.focalObject: The currently hovered or selected robot silhouette, cropped large enough to feel collectible.
concepts.emotionalHook: The first screen asks which machine deserves to be activated, creating curiosity through scale, material, and partial reveal.
concepts.whatIsHidden: Dense skill analysis, stat tables, and implementation details stay behind the selected forge panel.
concepts.whatIsAbsent: No beige catalog, no generic dark cyber grid, no badge soup, no terminal newspaper panels.
concepts.clicheAvoidance: Robotics is expressed through tactile specimen presentation rather than neon cyber fighter cards.
concepts.desireMechanism: Hover reveals a robot-specific trait and shifts the specimen into the main stage; selection locks it into the forge.
concepts.desktop1440Strategy: Large selected robot stage, compact roster rail, and a restrained forge inspector use width without inflating every element.
concepts.tablet768Strategy: Selected robot stays dominant above a two-column roster/inspector stack with preserved card zones.
concepts.mobile390Strategy: One dominant robot card appears first, followed by a swipeable roster and a clear choose action without horizontal page scroll.
concepts.failureMode: It fails if the specimen metaphor becomes a plain product gallery or hides selection reward.

concepts.name: Forge Loadout
concepts.visualMetaphor: A premium loadout bench where choosing a robot feels like preparing a specialized tool for deployment.
concepts.composition: The first viewport centers a robot loadout bay with selectable robot cards arranged as tool cartridges below.
concepts.focalObject: The loadout bay with the active robot, class signal, and one primary forge action.
concepts.emotionalHook: Selecting a robot feels like slotting a powerful tool into a forge and seeing it come alive.
concepts.whatIsHidden: Long descriptions, diagnostics, and skill breakdowns appear only after the robot is selected.
concepts.whatIsAbsent: No brochure detail page, no passive card grid, no generic dashboard metrics.
concepts.clicheAvoidance: It avoids the obvious robot-game fighter screen by using a crafted workshop/loadout metaphor.
concepts.desireMechanism: Each card changes the loadout bay material, action label, and preview stance so selection feels committed.
concepts.desktop1440Strategy: Wide layout uses bay, cartridge rail, and inspector as three distinct zones.
concepts.tablet768Strategy: The loadout bay remains top priority with a compact rail and collapsible inspector.
concepts.mobile390Strategy: The active robot bay comes first, then a horizontal cartridge selector with clear tap targets.
concepts.failureMode: It fails if the loadout bay becomes a static hero with inactive cards.

concepts.name: Signal Hunt
concepts.visualMetaphor: A discovery interface where robots are found through distinctive signal signatures instead of being listed like products.
concepts.composition: A large signal map or silhouette field sits behind three featured robot choices, with the selected robot resolving from signal to form.
concepts.focalObject: The robot signal resolving into a visible robot identity.
concepts.emotionalHook: The user wants to uncover which robot signal is rare, strange, or powerful.
concepts.whatIsHidden: Exact specs and long skill cards are hidden until the signal resolves through selection.
concepts.whatIsAbsent: No stat-first dashboard, no fighter labels, no grid texture as generic AI atmosphere.
concepts.clicheAvoidance: The robot theme becomes discovery and reveal rather than dark cyber decoration.
concepts.desireMechanism: Hover previews a signal personality; selection transforms it into a robot identity with a visible reward.
concepts.desktop1440Strategy: Desktop uses depth: signal field, featured choices, and a narrow resolved-details tray.
concepts.tablet768Strategy: Signal field remains readable while choices become a compact two-row roster.
concepts.mobile390Strategy: One signal/robot reveal dominates the screen, with three clear choices below.
concepts.failureMode: It fails if the signal effect becomes decorative motion that does not clarify selection.
